about: Every branch of the judgement, and the boundary on each side of it. A case here is one thing changed from the baseline, so a failure names the check that moved.

cases.name: a sound license
cases.why: the baseline every other case differs from by one thing

cases.name: an integrity check the host failed
cases.why: settled before anything else: a binary that is not what it should be is not asked what license it holds

cases.name: nothing registered
cases.why: no token to judge

cases.name: a revoked activation
cases.why: the stamp is read before the token it revokes, so revocation outlives a restart

cases.name: a token that cannot be read
cases.why: held apart from a token in another schema: this one is damaged and has to be replaced from its source

cases.name: a token in another schema
cases.why: read before the signature is computed: a format this deployment cannot read is not worth checking a signature over

cases.name: no key for the token's kid
cases.why: a token naming a key this deployment does not carry is refused, never checked against whatever key is at hand

cases.name: another product's license
cases.why: asked right after the signature and before the machine: if the token belongs to another product, whether the machine matches is not worth asking

cases.name: a machine the token does not name
cases.why: one of three collected matches, which is below half

cases.name: a machine that reports nothing
cases.why: refused rather than waved through: without an identifier the binding cannot be checked at all

cases.name: a container reading one identifier of two
cases.why: half of two is one, so a deployment that lost a mount keeps working

cases.name: the instant a license expires
cases.why: the expiry instant is still inside the window

cases.name: one second past expiry
cases.why: the grace period starts, and the deployment keeps serving while being told

cases.name: the last instant of the grace period
cases.why: thirty days after expiry is still inside it

cases.name: one second past the grace period
cases.why: settled here, without consulting a clock watermark or a heartbeat

cases.name: a development license past expiry
cases.why: the development channel has no grace period at all

cases.name: a license that carries no expiry
cases.why: a perpetual sale never stops being valid, so a clock long past the baseline's expiry settles nothing

cases.name: no expiry, on the development channel
cases.why: the channel decides the grace period, and there is no expiry for one to follow

cases.name: no expiry, a release above the ceiling
cases.why: never expiring is not entitlement to upgrade forever — the ceiling is judged the same way it is for a subscription

cases.name: a release above the ceiling
cases.why: the deployment keeps serving — a closed door is not an entitlement control — and grants nothing

cases.name: a clock moved back past the watermark
cases.why: the only reason to move a clock back past a recorded watermark is to reach an expiry that has already passed

cases.name: ordinary drift inside the tolerance
cases.why: a clock corrected backwards by an hour has not been tampered with

cases.name: a heartbeat on its deadline
cases.why: the deadline instant is still in time

cases.name: a heartbeat one second late
cases.why: the tolerance is the wider of the two windows, and past it the license denies

cases.name: a development license on any machine
cases.why: a wildcard binding is what makes a development license portable, and it is accepted on that channel only

cases.name: a license release 1.0.0 issued, in schema 1
cases.why: The first published format. Carries an expiry, which schema 2 later made optional. Frozen as it went out: a release that stops reading it revokes every license already sold under it.

cases.name: a token below the oldest schema this build reads
cases.why: the floor is the one place a release may declare earlier licenses dead, and it refuses them by the same door a newer schema is refused by
